questions.question: The paradox of Alankara and Svabhavokti in Indian Poetics / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Alankara (embellishment) – main source of poetic beauty – it separated poetic language from
  • ordinary language – Svabavokti (natural description) - if alankara was absolutely necessary
  • for poetry, then svabhavokti could not be accepted as poetry because it referred to expression
  • without embellishment – the relationship between embellishment and the thing embellished
  • existed naturally in alankara - svabavokti was unembellished expression (Kuntaka) – poems
  • containing only svabavokti without any figure of speech are also beautiful – opinions are
  • divided – some critics rejected. In contrast, others accepted it in some forms. [U] / [CO3]

questions.question: What are the major characteristics that distinguish English Romanticism from other literary periods? / [CO1]

  • first major Romantic poet – mystical and myth based - criticized emerging urban and
  • industrial society – highlighted social injustice and attacked dominance of rational thinking –

  • imagination – primary and secondary – suspension of disbelief - Shelley – imagination over
  • reason – elevated poetry’s importance – Keats – negative capability. [U] / [CO1]
